findings.title: website_name bypasses the existing anonymous TL0 privacy restriction
findings.body: `website` is explicitly listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so an anonymous viewer of a TL0 profile does not receive it. The newly added `website_name` attribute is not subject to that restriction, but is derived directly from the hidden website and can include both its host and path. As a result, anonymous clients receive profile URL information that the serializer intentionally withholds (for example, `example.com/private-profile`) even though `website` itself is absent. Add `website_name` to the same conditional visibility policy as `website` (and ensure its include predicate follows that policy).

findings.title: Sibling hostnames are treated as the same domain using an unsafe label-count heuristic
findings.body: For any two hostnames with more than two labels, this compares everything except the first label. That incorrectly treats unrelated registrable domains under multi-part public suffixes as the same domain: with an instance at `forum.github.io`, a website at `alice.github.io/private` will display `alice.github.io/private`, despite being a different site; the same occurs for hosts under `co.uk` and other public suffixes. The decision to expose the full path should use a public-suffix-aware registrable-domain comparison (or restrict it to exact hostname/known instance-domain relationships), rather than dropping the first DNS label.

findings.title: The website_name inclusion predicate is not named according to serializer convention
findings.body: Serializer conditional methods in this class use the `include_<attribute>?` form (for example, `include_email?` and `include_card_image_badge?`). This method is named `include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, so the serializer will not invoke it as the condition for `:website_name`; profiles without a website can therefore receive a `website_name: null` field instead of omitting it as intended. Rename it to `include_website_name?` and apply the same visibility condition as `website`.
